title: Guard clause in apply_discount silently skips discount for exactly $100.00
reasoning: The apply_discount function contains a guard clause `if amount > DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD` that acts as an implicit validator for whether the discount path should execute. For a cart of exactly $100.00, this guard evaluates to False (100.00 > 100.00 is False), silently falling through and returning the original amount unchanged — no exception, no log, just a silent no-op. The bug report confirms `discount_applied=false` with `subtotal=100.00`, which is exactly the behaviour of a guard clause that excludes the boundary value. The validate_coupon function and order_total pipeline have no other early-returns that affect this path; the only guard that can silently prevent the discount is this strict comparison.
evidence: Log shows subtotal=100.00 discount_applied=false — discount path was silently skipped, not errored
Cart of exactly $100.00 hits the boundary case; $120.00 cart passes the guard and receives discount correctly
validate_coupon returns True for None/empty coupon, so no early-return in order_total blocks the discount call
apply_discount uses `>` instead of `>=`, making the boundary value $100.00 fall through the guard without discount

patch.find: if amount > DISCOUNT_THRESHOLD:   # SEEDED BUG: should be >=
